main_text.p: Precept. Quibus deniq; eparest frigidum[?], ventri-culusq; eadem intemperie laborat, vel à ni-mio fragorum vsu abstinebunt, vel come-dent ea ex vino cum saccharo & cinnamo-mo.
main_text.head: De prunis.
main_text.p: Pruna feré omnia post Catonem cœpisse certum est. Plura sunt eorum genera, sa-pore, colore, figura & magnitudine distin-cta[?]. Principatum obtinent Damascena, quorum quedam nigra sunt, quedam rubent, quedam violacea cernuntur. Sic appellata à celeberrima urbe Damasco, alii vocant Syriaca: deportantur ficca in omnem feré terram, inq; coquinis magnatum non postremum tenent locum. Consici-tur ex his confectio, quæ diaprunum appellatur, ad febres ficcas commodissimum, ob humectan-di & refrigerandi vim. Recentia omnia aluum laxant, emolliunt, insigniter enim humectant probè matura, immatura enim acerbiora sunt, unde ob acriorem quendam qui illis inest, succum, crudum, intestina vellicant, fluxum, dy-sentericum excitant.
Eligenda autem quæ amplitudine, suavitate, saporisq; gratiā commendantur, ea enim ceteris plus alunt, vino aut mulso incocta.

page.notes: Precept. is a marginal note in the left margin. Doubtful readings: "eparest frigidum" (line reads as printed "epareftfrigidum", spacing and letters uncertain); "distin-cta" (word after the hyphen is partly unclear); "mulso" (last word of the final paragraph is uncertain). The drop initial P of "Pruna" is joined to the word. Printed "Veruns" at the foot is the catchword "Verum", partly cut off.
